questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

A Gita is considered / to be a dialogue between / the Pandava prince, Arjuna, / and Lord Krishna.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The main issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the article "**A**" before "**Gita**."
 
• The sacred text should be referred to with the definite article "**the**" instead of the indefinite article "**a**."
 
• The phrase should correctly read as "**The Gita is considered**."
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The Gita is considered to be a dialogue between the Pandava prince, Arjuna, and Lord Krishna."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "to be a dialogue between"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **2: "the Pandava prince, Arjuna"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **3: "and Lord Krishna"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

The team members will meet __on a airport__ at 7 a.m. tomorrow
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'at the airport'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is** grammatically incorrect**. Hence, the underlined part should be improved.
 
• Here,** 'at the airport'** should be used instead of **'on a airport'.**
 
• In the given context the preposition '**at**' means **'used to show where somebody/something is or where something happens**'.
 
 
• *Example: He was standing **at **the door.*
 
 
 
• The definite article '**the**' should be used instead of '**a**' because 'the' before a noun shows that what is referred to is already known to the speaker, listener, writer, and/or reader (it is the definite article). 
 
 
• *Example: We had to paint the apartment before we sold it. (The speaker and the listener know what apartment is being referred to.)

 ​*
 
 

**Correct Sentence:__** *The team members will meet** at the airport **at 7 a.m. tomorrow.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__** 

__
 
• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है। इसलिए, रेखांकित भाग में सुधार किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• यहां, **'on a airport'** के बजाय** 'at the airport' **का इस्तेमाल किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• दिए गए संदर्भ में preposition **'at' **यह दिखाने के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है कि कोई/कुछ कहां है या जहां कुछ होता है।
 
 
• ​*Example: He was standing at the door.*
 
 
 
• निश्चित Article '**the**' का प्रयोग '**a**' के स्थान पर किया जाना चाहिए।
 
• क्योंकि **Noun** से पहले '**the**' यह दर्शाता है कि जिसे संदर्भित किया गया है वह वक्ता, श्रोता, लेखक और/या पाठक को पहले से ही ज्ञात है (यह निश्चित लेख है)।
 
 
• *Example: We had to paint the apartment before we sold it. (*स्पीकर और श्रोता जानते हैं कि किस अपार्टमेंट को संदर्भित किया जा रहा है*)*

questions.question: Select the sentence with the most appropriate degree of adjective.

options.text: She is the talent of all musicians in the orchestra.
She is the talentedest musician in the orchestra.
She is more talented musician in the orchestra.
She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct way to express the highest degree of comparison **(superlative degree)** is by using **"the most + adjective"** for adjectives that are longer than one syllable.
 
• Option 4, "She is the most talented musician in the orchestra," is grammatically correct and expresses the idea appropriately.
 
• Other options contain grammatical errors:
 
 
• **Option 1:** "She is the talent of all musicians in the orchestra" is incorrect because "talent" is a noun, not a comparative adjective.
 
• **Option 2:** "She is the talentedest musician in the orchestra" is incorrect because "talentedest" is not a valid English word.
 
• **Option 3:** "She is more talented musician in the orchestra" is incorrect as it requires "the" before "more talented" to complete the comparison.
 
 

Correct sentence: *She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Degree:**

 
 
• Used to compare two things or people.
 
• For one-syllable adjectives, add "-er" (e.g., taller, smarter).
 
• For longer adjectives, use "more + adjective" (e.g., more talented, more beautiful).
 
 
 
• **Superlative Degree:**
 
 
• Used to compare one thing or person against all others in a group.
 
• For one-syllable adjectives, add "-est" (e.g., tallest, smartest).
 
• For longer adjectives, use "the most + adjective" (e.g., the most talented, the most beautiful).

questions.question: Select the option that has used the correct tense.

options.text: By the time we arrive at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
By the time we arrived at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
By the time we arrives at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
By the time we arriving at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.

questions.solution:
The correct option is: **2) By the time we arrived at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 2** is grammatically correct because it uses the correct tense sequence.
 
• The phrase **"By the time we arrived"** uses the **past simple tense**, which is appropriate for an action that is completed before another action in the past.
 
• The phrase **"they had been waiting"** uses the **past perfect continuous tense**, indicating that their waiting started earlier and continued until the time we arrived.
 
• This combination of past simple and past perfect continuous is the correct way to show the sequence of events.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **By the time we arrived at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Why the other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 1: **"By the time we arrive at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour."

 
 
• This option incorrectly uses the present tense "arrive" instead of the past tense "arrived." Since the sentence talks about an event that happens before another event in the past, the past tense "arrived" is required.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "By the time we arrives at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour."
 
 
• This option incorrectly uses "arrives", which is the present tense form for a singular subject (e.g., "he/she arrives"). Since the subject "we" is plural, the correct form should be "arrived" (past tense).
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "By the time we arriving at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour."
 
 
• This option incorrectly uses "arriving", which is the present participle form. To show a completed action in the past, the correct form is "arrived" (past simple).

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.**

________ you please help me with my computer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Could**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate **modal** for the given blank is '**Could**'.
 
• It is used for** informal/ friendly requests**.
 
 
• *Example: John **could** be the one who stole the money.*
 
 
 
• We know that "**Could**" is **a modal verb** used to express possibility or **past** ability as well as to make **suggestions and requests. **
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** ***Could** you please help me with my computer?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

 
• दिए गए रिक्त स्थान के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त मोडल '**Could**' है।
 
• इसका उपयोग **informal/ friendly requests** के लिए किया जाता है।
 
 
• *Example: John **could** be the one who stole the money.*
 
 
 
• हम जानते हैं कि "**Could**" एक **modal verb** है जिसका उपयोग संभावना या पिछली क्षमता को व्यक्त करने के साथ-साथ सुझाव और अनुरोध करने के लिए किया जाता है।
 
• अत: सही उत्तर **विकल्प 1** है।

questions.question:
**The given sentence contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment that contains the error.**

You look very tired; you would go to bed now.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'you would go'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'you should go'** will be used instead of** 'you would go'.**
 
• We use '**should**' to show obligation, give recommendations, or even an opinion.
 
 
• *Example: You **should** stop eating fast food.*
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *You look very tired; you should go to bed now.*

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into superlative degree.

No other mountain in the world is as high as the Mount Everest.

options.text: No other mountain is highest than Mount Everest.
Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
Mount Everest is higher than any other mountain in the world.
Mount Everest is high mountain in the world.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'B' i.e. Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the positive degree.
 
• The superlative degree is used to compare more than two things.
 
• The correct transformation follows this pattern:
 
 
• **Positive Degree:** No other mountain in the world is as high as Mount Everest.
 
• **Superlative Degree:** Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct Sentence: *Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Degree:** Mount Everest is higher than any other mountain in the world.
 
• **Positive Degree:** No other mountain in the world is as high as Mount Everest.
 
• In superlative degree transformation, we use "**the + superlative form**."
 
• Example:
 
 
• **Positive:** No other city is as crowded as Mumbai.
 
• **Superlative:** Mumbai is the most crowded city.

questions.question:
Select the option that changes the degree of comparison in the given sentence from superlative to positive without changing the meaning of the sentence.

Kalpana Ahuja is the tallest girl in the colony.

options.text: Many girls in the colony are taller than Kalpana Ahuja.
Kalpana Ahuja is as tallest as other girls of the colony.
No other girl in the colony is as taller as Kalpana Ahuja.
No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. would look .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of the** positive degree of comparison**, which is used to compare one item with another without indicating the highest degree.
 
• In a positive degree sentence, the structure is typically **"as + adjective + as"**.
 
• Option 4 correctly follows the structure **"No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja."** ensuring the comparison remains positive.

Correct sentence: *No other girl in the colony is as tall as Kalpana Ahuja.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Superlative Degree:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + verb + the + superlative adjective + noun.
 
• **Example:** She is the smartest student in the class.
 
• **Usage: **Describes the highest degree of a quality among three or more items.
 
 
 
• **Comparative Degree:**
 
 
• **Structure: **Subject + verb + comparative adjective + than + noun.
 
• **Example: **She is smarter than her brother.
 
• **Usage: **Compares two items, indicating a higher degree of a quality in one.

questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

He was studying in the __dimmer__ light.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. dim .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is incorrect as "dimmer" is the comparative form of "dim," and its usage suggests a comparison between two or more things.
 
• However, there is no comparison mentioned in the given sentence, so the correct form should be the positive degree "dim."
 
• The correct phrase should be "dim light."

Correct sentence: *He was studying in the dim light.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Degree of Adjectives Examples:**

 
 
• **Positive Degree:** Describes a quality without any comparison. Example: He prefers dim light for reading.
 
• **Comparative Degree:** Compares between two entities. Example: This room is dimmer than the other one.
 
• **Superlative Degree:** Describes the highest degree of a quality among three or more entities. Example: This is the dimmest room in the house.
